content: Postprandial angina pectoris refers to chest discomfort that arises after eating a meal. This condition is believed to result from an increase in vascular tone or a decrease in coronary blood flow. Any form of angina can manifest after meals due to heightened coronary vascular tone and reduced coronary blood flow. However, postprandial angina specifically occurs during physical exertion following a meal because of the increased oxygen demand of the heart muscle. This type of angina is almost always linked to the presence of significant atherosclerotic disease in the coronary arteries. The primary symptom of postprandial angina is chest discomfort that occurs during physical activity after eating. The management of postprandial angina is identical to the treatment approach for chronic stable angina.
